panels.title: Fetch success rate, by source_kind
panels.description: success / (success + failure), excluding not_modified — a 304 isn't a failure to poll, it's the fast path working as designed.

panels.title: Yield ratio, by source_kind
panels.description: docs/16 section 3.2 — new jobs / polls, the rolling EMA apps/collector/internal/interval already computes for scheduling. Low and falling is the earliest signal a source or an entire adapter has quietly broken.

panels.title: 304 ratio (conditional-GET hit rate), by source_kind
panels.description: not_modified / total. docs/06 section 5 targets 85% here — most polls should cost ~500 bytes, not a full response.

panels.title: Sources with an open circuit breaker
panels.description: circuit_open_until in the future — the source is being backed off after repeated failures, per docs/06's circuit-breaker predicate (also re-checked by the politeness gate before every fetch, independent of this).

targets.rawSql: select c.canonical_name as company, s.kind as source_kind, s.consecutive_failures, s.circuit_open_until, s.last_polled_at, s.url from source s join company c on c.id = s.company_id where s.circuit_open_until > now() order by s.circuit_open_until desc limit 50

panels.title: 20 worst-performing sources, by yield
panels.description: docs/16 section 8's own spec for this dashboard: "a table of the 20 worst-performing sources sorted by yield decline." Filtered to sources with at least 10 polls — a brand-new source's yield_ratio starts at 0 by construction (packages/db/queries/source.sql's UpdateSourceAfterPoll EMA), which isn't the same signal as an established source's yield actually dropping.

targets.rawSql: select c.canonical_name as company, s.kind as source_kind, s.yield_ratio, s.total_polls, s.total_jobs_found, s.total_new_jobs, s.consecutive_failures, s.status, s.last_polled_at from source s join company c on c.id = s.company_id where s.total_polls >= 10 order by s.yield_ratio asc limit 20
